question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(x+a), & -6\le x\le 2 \\ x-1, & x>2\end{aligned}
$$

 
is continuous at  $x=2,$ find the value of $a.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=2,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}g(x) & =g(2)=\operatorname{log}⁡(2+a),\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}(x-1) \\  & =2-1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=2,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}g(x) \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(2+a) & =1 \\ 2+a & ={10}^{1} \\ 2+a & =10 \\ a & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
